title: Load five glass slides into a staining rack
instruction: Move the five slides from the drying rack into the staining rack, one slide per slot.
context: Diagnostic histology and clinical laboratories move glass slides into a staining rack before the stain line; slides are held only by their edges so the specimen area is never touched, and a slide that falls flat or lands two to a slot ruins the run.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y to the left; arm bases at x 0, y +-0.305 m). Five loose soda-lime glass microscope slides (slide_1 to slide_5), each 75 mm (y) x 1.0 mm (x) x 25 mm (z), 5 g, pale blue-green glass colour (0.80, 0.88, 0.90), standing upright on a long edge with their 75 mm length along y. Fixed grey plastic slide drying rack (colour 0.55, 0.57, 0.60) centred at x 0.31 m, y +0.30 m: a 150 mm (x) x 45 mm (y) x 3 mm (z) floor slab resting on the table (slab top 0.7505 m) with six 45 mm long (y) x 10 mm tall (z) groove blocks on top (four inner blocks 26.0 mm wide along x, two end blocks 13.0 mm wide) whose gaps form five 4.0 mm wide grooves at 30 mm pitch along x at x = 0.25, 0.28, 0.31, 0.34, and 0.37 m. The five slides start standing upright in the five drying-rack grooves (bottom 1 mm above the slab top at spawn, settling onto it), overhanging the 45 mm rack by 15 mm at each end. Fixed white plastic staining rack (colour 0.92, 0.92, 0.90) centred at x 0.31 m, y +0.12 m: same 150 x 45 x 3 mm floor slab and five 4.0 mm grooves at 30 mm pitch along x (x = 0.25, 0.28, 0.31, 0.34, 0.37 m), with six 12 mm tall groove blocks whose groove mouths are chamfered (opening to 8.0 mm at the top and narrowing to the 4.0 mm groove body 4 mm down) and open ends so the slides' ends overhang by 15 mm per side. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The tilt of a slide is the angle between its local z axis (25 mm side) and world z. A slide is in staining-rack slot k (k = 1..5, centres at x = 0.25, 0.28, 0.31, 0.34, 0.37 m, y = +0.12 m) when its centre x is within 2.0 mm of slot k's centre, its centre y is within 10 mm of the rack's centre y (+0.12 m), its lowest point is within 3 mm of the rack slab's top (0.7505 m), and its tilt is under 10 degrees. If at any moment a slide's tilt exceeds 60 degrees (lying flat) or it goes off the table (centre below the table top 0.7475 m or beyond x -0.19 to 0.91 m, y -0.65 to +0.65 m), a '<slide> fell' violation is latched for that slide for the rest of the trial, and that slide counts 0 even if stood up again. Edge-only handling: the protected specimen area is, on both 75 x 25 mm faces, everything except the 12.5 mm at each end. If at any moment a gripper's fingers close across a slide's thickness (closing axis within 45 degrees of the face normal) with the slide between its open fingers and its pads over the protected area, a '<slide> face contact' violation is latched and that slide counts 0 for the rest of the trial. In real trials the gripper pads are inked on a washable-ink stamp pad before each trial, and any ink mark inside a slide's protected area after the run makes that slide count 0. If two or more slides are in the same slot, all of them in that slot count 0. Score (SCORE_OVER = 'end', taken at the trial's last step): 0.2 per slide that is in a rack slot, at rest (linear speed under 1 cm/s and angular speed under 0.5 rad/s), has not fallen during the trial, is alone in its slot, and has both robot grippers' tool centre points at least 3 cm from every point of the slide (released) (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, or 1.0). The trial succeeds and ends early with score 1.0 when all five slides are counted and stays so for 1 s.
fidelity: Each 1 mm glass slide is a rigid box with no breakage, and racks are built from fixed rigid boxes (staining ribs use compound chamfered mouths opening from 4.0 mm to 8.0 mm at the top). Contacts use friction 1.2 (dynamic 1.0), holding a 5 g slide by its 25 x 1 mm ends. Groove pitch is 30 mm instead of 6-8 mm because the simulated fingers are ~27 mm wide and would hit neighbouring slides at 8 mm pitch.
